Commentary.Commentary: The players are out in the middle. 28 overs left for the day. How many wickets can New Zealand get with the new ball? Rory Burns and Dominic Sibley open up for England. Tim Southee to start off proceedings to Burns.
The wicket still seems to be a good one to bat on but scoreboard pressure can get to the English batters. An interesting passage of play awaits.

Now then, England will probably bat to save this game. They need to take it session by session. Their first aim will be to get through today with not a lot of damage being done. New Zealand on the other hand, have around 28 overs today and they would look to take as many wickets as possible.

England at the moment will be mentally and physically drained! They have bowled over 200 overs. Their bowling throughout looked flat. Not a lot you can write about a bowling attack which has failed to bundle out an opposition in two days. If you still have to pick one bowler who impressed, then it is Sam Curran. Overall, it is a performance the English bowlers would want to forget.

The stars for the Kiwis, BJ Watling, Mitchell Santner and Colin de Grandhomme. Nicholls and Williamson also played well but when the two were dismissed, the Kiwis were on the back foot. However then the fightback started. First Watling and Colin de Grandhomme took the hosts to safer shores and then Santner and Watling with a massive 261-run stand took New Zealand right on top. The wicket keeper scored a double ton and Santner managed to get his maiden first Test ton.

NEW ZEALAND HAVE FINALLY DECLARED! Yes, you have read it right, they HAVE DECLARED after batting for around 2 days. They have probably batted long enough to ensure they can't lose the game from here and the only team who could win this one is themselves. They have a lead of 262 now and just less than 4 sessions to get the 10 wickets they need of England.

On off, kept out.

Maybe a few overs, one thing we can assure is, we are in for some fun now. Southee will be on strike and he will be facing Jack Leach.

So the Kiwis have batted yet another full session! However, this time around, they have scored at a very brisk rate. They managed to score 138 runs in 27 overs. Right from the onset both Santner and Watling started off in a positive manner. They were finding the fence regularly, especially the former who got to his maiden Test ton. The pair brought up the250-run stand too between them before the left-hander was dismissed. Watling though continued and he got to his double ton. The lead is 237 now so the only thing we believe the hosts are playing for is to take the lead to the 250-run mark. Will they be declaring then or will they bat for another hour or will they be declaring immediately? A lot of questions to be answered and they will be in a while. Stay tuned.

Welcome back for the post lunch session. New Zealand  batsmen BJ Watling and Mitchell Santner are out in the middle. England players are on the field. Stuart Broad to start the session with the ball. How many more runs will New Zealand add or when will the declaration come? Let's find out. Here we go....
... Day 4, session 2 ...

Just the 58 runs in this session! Not sure, just not sure with what approach did the Kiwis come out. One would have thought they would be looking to score some quick runs and probably be in a position where they can think of declaration early in the second session but that was not the case. They were happy to go along at a snail's pace, yes they did not lose a wicket but did not score a lot of runs too. Santner has managed to get to his fifty and Watling is nearing his 150. The question is how many more runs are they looking to add? What will their approach be after the break? Stay tuned in a bit to find out.

We are all set to begin. The centurion BJ Watling is accompanied by Mitchell Santner in the middle. The England Players have also taken their respective fielding positions. Jofra Archer to start the proceedings with the ball. We are set to go...

Hello and welcome to day 4 of this intriguing Test match. Till now we are not clear of where this Test match is heading, courtesy a solid fightback from the New Zealand middle order. To start with, let's applaud the unsung hero of New Zealand's innings. Yes, you guessed it right, it's none other than BJ Watling. He came to the crease at a time when New Zealand were reeling at conceding a huge lead but changed the course of the match with his hard fought innings. The hosts are now in a position where if they have one or probably a little more than one good session, then losing the game for them will probably become improbable. A lead of around 150 is what they will be looking for before declaring. England on the other hand, need to get the remaining wickets quickly or they will be batting under tremendous pressure in their second innings. An exciting day awaits.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Day 4 can probably define which way this game is heading towards! New Zealand will probably look to take their lead upto the 150-run mark or so and then try and bundle England out as quickly as possible. The tourists on the other hand, need to pick the remaining wickets quickly and then concentrate on their batting. An important day awaits, do join us at 1100 local (2200 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye!

The England bowlers, just like the Kiwi bowlers had to toil hard. However, the English batters threw it away in their innings but New Zealand did not make the same mistakes. Also, England did not help themselves in the field too. Watling was dropped early on by Stokes which really cost them big. Also, the visitors were very sloppy and it seemed they weren't up for it on Day 3. Strange actually, seeing the position they were in at the end of Day 2, you would expect them to come out all guns blazing but that was not the case and now they find themselves behind the 8 ball game.

A huge round of applause for the hero of today, BJ Watling as he walks off. The English players walk upto him and shake his hand. He deserves every bit of ovation he is getting, that is how good his knock has been. He is the major reason why New Zealand are in the position they are. Credit though has to be given to Nicholls, Colin de Grandhomme and Santner too. First it was Henry who hung out there with Watling, the two managed to steady the ship after New Zealand were struggling at 127 for 4. However, the two partnerships after that is what took the Kiwis on top. First, Colin de Grandhomme and Watling, the former scored an excellent half ton. The pair added 119 and the runs were also scored at a decent rate. That stand took the Kiwis to safer shores and then, the association between Santner and Watling which is still not done, has New Zealand in a commanding position at the end of Day 3.

Welcome back for the final session of the day. New Zealand are on track to take a lead here. The two batters who have kept New Zealand in the hunt, BJ Watling and Colin de Grandhomme walk in to the middle. England players take their positions. What a session for the Kiwis! This stand between Watling and Grandhomme has completely turned the tide in the hosts' favour. Before entering this session, 353 seemed farfetched for the home side but now, they are in a good position to take a handy lead. The two batters have looked untroubled and both will be eyeing a ton and that is exactly what New Zealand want. England on the other hand, need to break this stand and that too quickly or the game might just slip out of their hands. An important last session awaits.

Welcome back for the  second session. The England players are on the field. New Zealand batsmen BJ Watling and Colin de Grandhomme also come out. England take the second new ball and it will be Sam Curran who will use it first up. To know what is in store in this session, here we go....
... Day 3, Session 2 ...

Early wickets is what England were looking for entering Day 3 but Watling and Henry showed great grit and determination and built a solid stand.Scoring was not easy but the two did well to grind it out. However, a master stroke from Root to get himself on broke the 70-run stand. He could have had both the set-batters had Stokes not dropped Watling. That missed opportunity could prove costly as BJ is nearing a half ton now and will be eyeing to make it big. He is well-supported by Colin so far and New Zealand will hope the two continue. England know, they need one wicket and they are into the bowling all-rounders. Will the hosts continue their fightback or will the visitors continue to dominate. Join us in a while to find out.

Curran is still getting the ball to do a bit here! He gets this one to tail back in from middle, Watling works it through square leg for one.
Length ball angling on the pads, Nicholls looks to flick it through mid-wicket but fails to time his shot. The ball hits his pads. A stifled appeal from the bowler but nothing from his teammates.
Nicholls plays a forward defensive shot to this length ball outside off.

A gentle length ball around off, Watling defends it to the off side.

Have England missed a trick here by not starting with Jofra Archer? A good looking drive but for no runs! Fuller and on off, it is hit to mid off. Another maiden, England keeping it nice and tight.
Fuller and on off, Nicholls strokes it to the man at mid off.
A nice bumper, Nicholls ducks under it.

The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

A leave to end as this is also bowled outside off. A maiden but not a threatening one.
Goes wide of the crease and angles it into the batter, BJ keeps it out.
In the 5th stump channel, it is left alone nicely.
On a length and around off, Watling lunges and keeps it out.
Another delivery outside off, it is left alone. It goes on the bounce to the keeper. Signs of the wicket slowing up even more?
On a good length and outside off, Watling makes a leave.
Henry brings out a solid front foot defense to this length ball on off.
Nicholls blocks this length ball around off towards the off side.
Nicholls drives this length ball on off to mid on.
Length ball and keeping low outside off, Nicholls shoulders arms to it.
Nicholls drives this length ball outside off to covers.

Fuller one and on off, Nicholls looks to flick it through the leg side but gets hit on the pads. The England players appeal but the umpire is unmoved. Probably it was swinging too much down the leg side.
Length ball  outside off, Watling lets it be.
Length and outside off, Watling is happy leave it.

Outside off, left alone.
Length and on the pads, Nicholls flicks it off his pads towards fine leg and scampers for a single. 150 up for New Zealand.

Stuart Broad to start from the other end.
Outside off, left alone.
Good length and outside off, Watling lets it be.

Length ball outside off, Left alone.
Good length and around off, Nicholls pushes it off the back foot towards mid-wicket for the first runs off the day.
Length and around off, Nicholls pushes it to covers. Nicholls shows that he is alright after being hit by Archer bouncer the other day.

We are all set to begin Day 3. BJ Watling and Henry Nicholls are out in the middle and will resume their innings. England players also get on the field as they take their fielding positions. Sam Curran will start the proceedings with the ball. Here we go...

Welcome to Day 3, often referred to as the happening day in a Test match. Happening means that we will get a clear picture of where the Test match will be heading. New Zealand are still 209 runs behind the English total of 353. With 6 wickets in hand New Zealand will want a couple of good partnerships to get them closer to the English total if not surpass it. Whereas, England would want to gain a substantial lead and put the hosts on the back foot. They would also look to get a couple of quick wickets to keep themselves ahead in this contest. All in all an action-packed day awaits us. Do join to know whether New Zealand stage a fightback or will England continue their good work in this Test?
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

Majority of the day though was dominated by the hosts but still it is the visitors who will sleep better today. Earlier, a collapse saw England being 8 down even before they crossed the 300-run mark. However, Buttler's knock took them over the 350-run mark which people still believed to be short. In reply, the Kiwi batters did get off to starts but no one could make it count. Sam Curran was the star with the ball for the visitors as he got two important wickets. New Zealand now trail by 209 runs, they do still do have batting to come but everybody will have to contribute. England on the other hand, will want to repeat what they did in the last session and hope they can get a good lead. Join us for all the action on Day 3 at 1100 local (2200 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye!

Advantage England without a doubt! A tremendous session for them, three wickets is what they got which included two of New Zealand's best batters, Taylor and Williamson. However, it all started after Raval's dismissal. The opener played a rash shot which saw his downfall. Before that, he along with Williamson after the loss of Latham were going along really well but once he fell, New Zealand kept losing wickets at regular intervals which sees them behind the 8 ball game. Watling and Nicholls are fighting it out and are playing well but there is still a long way to go for them.
Quicker and on off, Watling goes back and keeps it out. The last ball is negotiated and THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 2!
On the pads, Nicholls works it around the corner for one.
Flatter and on off, this is pushed towards cover.
On the pads, Nicholls looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
Flatter and on middle, Nicholls pushes it to mid on.
Flatter and on middle, this is pushed down to long on for one.
Joe Root comes on. His main aim to get himself on is to bowl one quickly and somehow slip in another one from Archer.
Another short one to end! It is ducked under. End of a nasty over by Archer.
That has been played well again! One more short ball on middle, Nicholls does well to play it down with soft hands.
Another top bumper! It takes off after pitching. Nicholls just about evades it.
One more short one but this is down the leg side, it is left alone. Three short ones now, the full ball is coming.
Well played! Archer goes short again, Nicholls watches it closely and then works it straight to short leg.
Out comes the physio to have a look! Nicholls is taking his time and rightly so. Luckily though he is up on his feet and seems fine. Also, change of helmets for Henry. He is all fine to continue now.

BOOM! How many times have we seen Archer do this? He has hit Nicholls flush on the helmet. Shorter and on middle, it is quick. Nicholls has no time to get out of the way and it hits the side part of the helmet.
Watling defends this flighted ball off the front foot.
Full on middle, Nicholls sweeps it through square leg for a run.

Henry cuts this short ball outside off to point.
Nicholls defends this length ball off his back foot.

A rib-tickler this time, it is worked down to fine leg for one.
One more short ball, Nicholls again ducks under it.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
A bumper and it is ducked under.
Well played! Shorter and on middle, it keeps on rising. Nicholls does well to play it onto the ground with soft hands.
Shorter one on the body, it is ducked under.
Jofra Archer is back on! He has bowled short spells till now and this is probably another one. Can he pick a wicket.
A flatter delivery to end on off, Watling goes back and keeps it out.
Full and on off, Watling pushes it to covers.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On the stumps, Watling lunges and keeps it out.
Flatter and on off, Watling pushes it to covers.

The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
A huge shout but not given! An inside edge saved Nicholls there. Curran bowls this full and straight on middle, Nicholls looks to drive but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Close! Curran goes fuller this time around off, Nicholls pushes at it with hard hands. He gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Back of a length again and on off, Nicholls pushes it towards cover where the fielder dives and stops it well.
Back of a length and on off, Nicholls guides it to point.

On the stumps, Nicholls defends it out nicely.
Outside off, the batter does not fiddle with it.

The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery

Bumper to end the over. Nicholls ducks under it.

Fuller one on the pads, Henry flicks it towards square leg and takes a couple.
Length and on off, Henry drives it to mid off.
Length ball on off, Nicholls defends it off the back foot.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
On middle, it is kept out.

Flatter and on off, it is kept out.
Full and on middle, pushed towards cover by Watling for a single.
Loopy ball outside off, Watling looks to drive but gets an inside edge on the pads.
Flighted around off, pushed towards cover.
Full and on off, Nicholls pushes it back to the bowler.

OUT! CAUGHT! Williamson gets out after his fifty. New Zealand are is a spot of bother as their batting mainstay is out of here. Curran bowls one on a length and generates some extra bounce on that one. Williamson looks to leave the ball but is late to react as the ball takes the glove and lobs towards Ben Stokes in the slips. Stokes dives in front and takes easiest of the catches.

Curran bowls one outside off, Williamson just opens the face of the bat at the last moment and runs it down though the slips and into the third man fence. Length and on off, Henry blocks it out.

Full and on off, Henry defends it back to the bowler.
Length and outside off, Kane taps it towards point and takes a single.
Length and on off, Henry blocks it off the back foot and into the ground.
FOUR! What a shot to get off the mark. Stokes goes full and on the pads, Nicholls flicks it off his pads through the mid-wicket region. The ball races away to the fence for a bounday.

Bumper going down leg, Williamson ducks under it.

Outside off, left alone.

Good length and on off, Nicholls guides it to the man at point.

Henry Nicholls walks out in the middle. He needs to stay with his skipper in the middle if New Zealand are to get closer to the English score.
DRINKS BREAK!

Length delivery outside off, Williamson does not play at it.

Length and on off, Taylor cuts it to point.
Fuller one outside off, Taylor blocks it off the toe-end of the bat and back to the bowler.
Length delivery around off, Taylor blocks it off the back foot.

Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
Floats it up on off, Williamson strokes it through covers for one. 50-run stand also comes up between Williamson and Raval. New Zealand would want them to continue and bat through.
Raval defends this length ball towards square leg.
Good length and on off, Raval blocks it off the back foot.
Length and around off, raval blocks it to the off side.
Good length and on off, Raval defends it.
Length and around off, Williamson pushes it through covers. The fielder from the covers and gives it a chase and saves a run for his team. The batsmen in the meantime take three.

FOUR! Lucky , very lucky. Broad bowls a fuller length ball and Williamson goes chasing it. The ball goes off the outside edge between the slips and gully. The ball races to the third man fence for a bounday.
Outside off, left alone.
Shorter and quicker on middle, Raval goes back and clips it to mid-wicket.

On middle, this is worked to mid-wicket.

Good length ball outside off, Kane taps it to point.

Length and outside off, Williamson watches the ball closely as he lets it through.

Flatter and on off, Raval stays back and works it to mid-wicket.
For the second time in a row Raval plays it to the fielder at mid on.
Floats it up on off, Raval plays it to mid on.
Jack Leach to bowl from the other end.
Outside off, KW does not fiddle with it.
That came back in a long way! Excellent delivery. This starts on off and comes back in late. Williamson looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
Goes back to bowling length and on off, Williamson prods forward and defends it.

Welcome back for the final session of Day 2. Joe Root leads his team out and has a few words of advice before they disperse on the field. Kane Williamson and Jeet Raval both walk out to the middle to resume their innings. Stuart Broad to start proceedings for the visitors. Here we go...
... Day 2, Session 3 ...

For England, Sam Curran has been impressive, he got the ball to move and also has a wicket to his name. Archer and Broad did not get a lot of assistance from the surface and Leach has begun decently. The one-odd ball is staying low or turning but nothing threatening at the moment. The visitors will hope for a wicket or two quickly after the break. Will they get it? Stay tuned to find out.

Good length and on off, this is kept out.

Outside off, Kane lets it be.
Length and on off, KW blocks it to mid on.

Outside off, it is left alone.
Now a couple! Shorter and around off, Williamson plays it late down towards third man and takes two.

FOUR! First boundary for the New Zealand skipper! Shorter in length and outside off, Williamson stands tall and punches it through covers for a boundary. Trademark Williamson this, he is very strong through that region.
Williamson retains the strike with a push through covers.
Fuller one and on the pads, Raval works it to fine leg and takes a single.
Fuller one on the pads, Williamson gets off the mark with a flicks towards mid-wicket.
Coming from round the wicket, Archer bowls one on a length and KW defends it back to the bowler.
Fuller one on middle, Williamson defends it to the leg side.
Back of a length and on off, Raval plays it to the mid-wicket region for a single.
Jofra Archer has change of ends.
Outside off, it is left alone.
On middle, this is worked towards mid-wicket.
A bumper to welcome the Kiwi skipper, Williamson ducks under it.
Kane Williamson, the skipper walks out.

OUT! LBW! England draw first blood and that too early. The bowling change has worked wonders for the visitors. A big wicket as Latham can play long innings. Yes, there were two noises there but it was of the bat hitting the pad. It is a full delivery around off, it tails back in late. Latham tries to defend but does so outside the line, the ball hits the front pad. A huge shout and up goes the finger. Hot Spot though does show a mark on the inside edge and then replays later on show, Latham might just have hit his pad and the ball together. Not sure though as the replays seem very confusing. Latham too might not have understood as he would have felt he hit the pad and not the ball. Latham could consider himself unlucky.
Outside off, Latham does not fiddle with it.
Very little movement first up! It lands on middle and straightens a touch. Latham gets right behind the line and keeps it out.
Sam Curran is on! First change for England! It will be interesting to see if he gets some movement.

FOUR! Beautiful drive from the left hander. Broad overpitches and Raval just leans on and times his drive to perfection as he gets it past the mid off fielder. The ball races to the long on fence for a boundary. First boundary off the bat.

Ripper from Broad! He bowls one on a length and around off and brings the ball back in. Latham looks to defend but the ball goes past it inside edge and over the stumps. Jos Buttler safely collects the ball into his mitts.
Good length ball outside off, Latham  taps it towards covers and takes off for a quick single.
1 run.
Outside off, Latham lets it be.
Length ball around off, Latham blocks it into the ground.
Back of a length and around off, Raval looks to defend but gets hit high on the thigh pads. The ball goes to the off side.
On a length and outside off, Raval blocks it to the off side.
Good length and around off, Jeet defends it to the leg side.
Bouncer down the leg side, Jeet looks uninterested as he ducks under it.
Length and on off, Raval defends it with a solid back foot defense.
Length and outside off, it is left alone.
Attacks the stumps this time, Latham gets right behind the line and keeps it out. Another maiden by Broad.
One more delivery outside off, Latham need not play at those.
Bowls this one outside off, Latham lets it be. Not getting the movement the Kiwi bowlers were getting. However, both the English bowlers are more of a hit the deck bowlers. Sam Curran maybe.
Down the leg side this time, Latham misses the flick shot.
This is on the pads, Latham looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
OHHH! That wasn't far from the off pole. This lands outside off, Latham lets it be. The ball not only stays low but comes in as well, misses the off pole but by not a lot.
A little too straight, Latham works it through square leg. It does not have the legs to get to the fence but the batters take three.
Just outside off, Latham does not fiddle with it.
Shorter and on off, Tom stays back and keeps it out.
Another length delivery on off, Raval drops it towards cover and takes one.
Outside off, it is left alone.
This is on the pads, Latham works it towards deep backward square leg for one.
Good length and going down the leg side. Raval gets inside the line and lets the ball through.
Back of a length and on the pads, Jeet flicks it to mid-wicket.
Good length and around middle and off, Raval defends it to the leg side.
Length and around off, Raval drives it to covers.
Length and outside off, Raval shoulders arms to it.
Good length and on off, it comes back in a touch. Raval looks to defend but it goes off the inner half towards square leg.
A good nut to end! This lands on off and then moves away. Latham thinks of playing at it but then bails out. An expensive first by Archer.
Raval is off the mark now! Archer continues to bowl short and on off, Raval opens the face of the bat and gets it past gully for one.
Latham is off the mark now! Archer bowls this slightly shorter around off, Latham goes back and guides it past backward point for three.

FOUR BYES! That kept going, going and going! A shorter in length delivery around off, it kept moving away even after passing the batter. Buttler moves across and tries to catch it but it hits the finger tips and rolls to the third man fence. New Zealand are underway courtesy four byes.
Another short one and on middle, Latham ducks under it.
Shorter and on middle, Latham stands tall and keeps it out.
Jofra Archer to bowl from the other end.
Another leave as the last ball too is outside off. A maiden to begin with by Broad but not a threatening one.
That came back in a long way! This starts from way outside off. Seeing that, Raval lets it be. It comes in a long way and goes close past the off pole.
This is bowled outside off, Raval does not fiddle with it.
On the fuller side this time but not a lot of movement on this one, Raval prods forward and keeps it out.
Shorter again and on off, Raval stands tall and defends it onto the ground.
Broad starts off with a length delivery around off, some movement into the batter. Raval gets right behind the line and keeps it out.
